Anna May Wong was the first Chinese American movie star and the first Asian American actress to gain international recognition. 1932

Anna May Wong (January 3, 1905 – February 3, 1961) was a 2nd generation American from Los Angeles whose long and varied career spanned across continents, languages and silent film, sound film, television, stage and radio. Wong became a fashion icon and had achieved international stardom by 1924. Frustrated by the stereotypical supporting roles she reluctantly played in Hollywood, Wong left for Europe in the late 1920s, where she starred in several notable plays and films. There she became very good friends with Marlene Dietrich and Leni Riefenstahl. This particular image was a publicity still taken for the film Shanghai Express in which she starred with Dietrich.
